# Field Service Scheduling — Product Requirements

## Background
Our field technicians are scheduled by phone. Dispatchers keep a spreadsheet, and customers do
not know when a technician will arrive. This document describes the first release of a scheduling
product for the operations team.

## Goals
- Let dispatchers assign jobs to technicians in one screen.
- Show customers an arrival window of two hours.
- Track job status from assignment to completion.

## Personas
- Dispatcher: assigns and reschedules jobs.
- Technician: sees today's route and updates job status.
- Customer: receives the arrival window by SMS.

## Functional requirements

### Job intake
1. A dispatcher can create a job with a customer name, address, skill and priority.
2. Jobs appear in a queue sorted by priority, then by requested date.
3. A job can be edited until a technician starts it.

### Assignment
4. The scheduler proposes technicians whose skills match the job and who are free in the time window.
5. A dispatcher can override the proposal and pick any active technician.
6. Assigning a job notifies the technician by push notification.

### Technician mobile view
7. The technician sees today's jobs in route order with the customer address.
8. The technician can mark a job as started, paused, or completed.
9. Completing a job asks for a short note and optional photos.

### Customer notification
10. When a job is assigned, the customer receives an SMS with a two-hour arrival window.
11. Rescheduling sends a new window and cancels the previous one.

### Reporting
12. Operations can export a weekly report of jobs per technician and average completion time.

## Non-functional requirements
- The mobile view must work on a phone with a weak connection.
- Every job status change is audited with user and timestamp.
- Customer phone numbers are personal data and must not appear in logs.

## Out of scope for this release
- Route optimisation beyond skill and availability.
- Billing and invoicing.
- C

options.extraInstructions: Keep the plan minimal: one sprint and at most three tasks.

project.name: Mode Matrix Fallback
project.description: A field service scheduling product that lets operations dispatchers create and assign jobs to field technicians from one screen, while technicians work their route on mobile and customers receive a two-hour SMS arrival window. The first release replaces the dispatcher spreadsheet and gives the operations team status tracking, audit coverage and a weekly report.

sprints.name: Sprint 1
sprints.goal: Deliver the first release end to end: dispatcher job intake and assignment, technician mobile status updates, and customer SMS arrival windows with a weekly export.

epics.title: Job intake and assignment
epics.description: Dispatchers create jobs, see a priority-ordered queue, receive skill/availability proposals, override them, and notify the technician.

epics.title: Technician mobile execution
epics.description: Technicians see today's route on a phone with weak connectivity and move jobs through started, paused and completed with audit and evidence.

epics.title: Customer notification and reporting
epics.description: Assigned and rescheduled jobs trigger SMS arrival windows, and operations exports weekly per-technician performance data.

items.title: Create, prioritise and assign jobs from the dispatcher screen
items.description: Give dispatchers one screen to create a job with customer name, address, skill and priority, see jobs queued by priority then requested date, edit a job until a technician starts it, accept or override the proposed technician, and trigger a technician push notification on assignment.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a dispatcher on the job screen, when they submit name, address, skill and priority, then the job is saved and appears in the queue.
Given several open jobs, when the queue renders, then jobs are ordered by priority first and requested date second.
Given a job whose technician has not started it, when the dispatcher edits and saves, then the change is persisted.
Given a job already started by a technician, when the dispatcher opens it, then editing is blocked with a clear message.
Given a job with skill and time window, when the dispatcher opens assignment, then only technicians with matching skills and availability are proposed.
Given a proposal, when the dispatcher selects any active technician instead, then the override is accepted and saved as the assignee.

subtasks.title: Design job intake form and queue layout
acceptanceCriteria: Form fields name, address, skill and priority are specified.
Queue sort order is documented as priority then requested date.

subtasks.title: Implement job create and edit with the started-job lock
acceptanceCriteria: Job create persists all four fields.
Edit is rejected once the job status is started.

subtasks.title: Implement priority-ordered queue query
acceptanceCriteria: Queue returns jobs sorted by priority then requested date.
Sorting is covered by a test with at least five mixed jobs.

subtasks.title: Implement skill and availability matching proposal
acceptanceCriteria: Proposal excludes technicians whose skills do not match.
Proposal excludes technicians busy in the job time window.

subtasks.title: Implement dispatcher override of the proposed technician
acceptanceCriteria: Any active technician can be chosen manually.
The chosen technician is stored as the assignee.

subtasks.title: Send push notification to the assigned technician
acceptanceCriteria: Assignment triggers one push notification to the technician.
Notification failure is retried and surfaced to the dispatcher.

subtasks.title: Write job status change audit record with user and timestamp
acceptanceCriteria: Each status or assignment change stores user id and UTC timestamp.
Audit records cannot be edited or deleted from the app.

subtasks.title: End-to-end test of the intake and assignment flow
acceptanceCriteria: Test covers create, queue order, edit lock, proposal, override and notification.
Test runs in CI on every merge.

items.title: Technician mobile route view and job status updates
items.description: Let a technician see today's jobs in route order with the customer address and move each job through started, paused and completed, including a short completion note and optional photos. The view must stay usable on a weak phone connection and every change is audited.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a technician with jobs today, when they open the app, then jobs are listed in route order with the customer address.
Given an assigned job, when the technician taps started, paused or completed, then the new status is saved and visible on reload.
Given a job being completed, when no completion note is entered, then submission is blocked until a short note is provided.
Given a job being completed, when photos are attached or skipped, then the completion is saved either way.
Given a weak or lost connection, when the technician changes a status, then the change is queued locally and synced when the connection returns.
Given any status change, when it is saved, then an audit record with technician, timestamp and previous status exists.

subtasks.title: Design today's route list and status action layout
acceptanceCriteria: Route order and address display are specified.
Started, paused, completed states are shown distinctly.

subtasks.title: Implement today's route list from assignment data
acceptanceCriteria: Only jobs assigned to the signed-in technician for today are returned.
List renders in route order with address.

subtasks.title: Implement status transitions and completion note with photos
acceptanceCriteria: Started, paused and completed transitions are persisted.
Completion requires a note and accepts optional photos.

subtasks.title: Implement offline queue and resync for status changes
acceptanceCriteria: Status changes made offline are stored on device.
Queued changes are sent in order when the connection returns.

subtasks.title: Add audit record for each mobile status change
acceptanceCriteria: Audit stores technician, timestamp and previous status.
A failing audit write blocks the status change.

subtasks.title: Test mobile flow on a throttled connection
acceptanceCriteria: Flow completes on a 200 kbps simulated connection.
Offline changes sync without duplicates.

items.title: Customer SMS arrival window, rescheduling and weekly operations report
items.description: When a job is assigned, send the customer an SMS with a two-hour arrival window; when it is rescheduled, send a new window and cancel the previous one. Provide operations a weekly export of jobs per technician and average completion time, keeping customer phone numbers out of logs.
acceptanceCriteria: Given an assigned job, when assignment completes, then the customer receives an SMS containing a two-hour arrival window.
Given a rescheduled job, when the new window is saved, then the customer receives a new SMS and the previous window is cancelled.
Given an SMS send failure, when the request is retried, then the failure is retried at least twice and reported to operations.
Given a weekly report export, when operations requests it, then it lists jobs per technician and average completion time.
Given any log line written by the system, when it is inspected, then customer phone numbers are absent or masked.

subtasks.title: Select SMS provider and define the two-hour window message format
acceptanceCriteria: Provider and credentials approach are agreed.
Message template includes the two-hour arrival window.

subtasks.title: Implement SMS send on assignment with retry and error reporting
acceptanceCriteria: One SMS per assignment is sent.
Failures retry twice and raise an operations alert.

subtasks.title: Implement reschedule SMS and cancellation of the previous window
acceptanceCriteria: Reschedule sends a new window.
The previous window is marked cancelled and not reused.

subtasks.title: Implement phone number masking in logs and error payloads
acceptanceCriteria: Phone numbers are masked in application logs.
A test asserts no raw phone number appears in log output.

subtasks.title: Implement weekly report of jobs per technician and average completion time
acceptanceCriteria: Export covers a full week and groups by technician.
Average completion time is computed from started to completed timestamps.

subtasks.title: Test the notification and reporting path end to end
acceptanceCriteria: Assignment, reschedule and export are covered by an automated test.
Masking assertion is part of the test suite.

assumptions: The requisitioner's sizing request is honoured: this release is planned as a single 2-week sprint with three items that merge the twelve functional requirements.
An SMS gateway provider exists and can be integrated within the sprint; the specific vendor is not named in the document.
Job status changes are stored as discrete states (assigned, started, paused, completed) with timestamps for audit and reporting.
Technicians and dispatchers already have accounts and can be marked active or inactive in the platform.
Skill matching uses a simple technician-skill list rather than route optimisation, which the document places out of scope.
Route order for the mobile view is derived from the technician's job sequence for the day; no map routing engine is built.
Push notifications use a standard mobile push service already available to the team.
The weekly report is delivered as a downloadable file; no dashboards are built in this release.
risks: Folding all twelve requirements into one sprint leaves no buffer for the SMS provider integration or mobile offline work.
Weak-connection behaviour on the technician phone is hard to verify without real field devices and network conditions.
Skill and availability matching may produce poor proposals if technician availability is not kept accurate, pushing dispatchers to constant overrides.
SMS deliverability and carrier latency could make the two-hour arrival window unreliable for customers.
Storing completion photos may grow storage fast and is not sized in this plan.
Audit and phone-number masking requirements can be forgotten on new code paths without enforced tests.
The weekly report depends on completion timestamps that only exist once technicians adopt the mobile flow.
No explicit error-handling or alerting owner is defined, so failed notifications could go unnoticed between operations and engineering.
